1.note: Micah is using the words **And I said** to introduce a direct quotation of what he said to the leaders. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

Here, **heads** represents the leaders of the people and the name **Jacob** the people of Israel who were all descendants of the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel.. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [leaders of the people of Israel]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

Micah is using the question form to rebuke the leaders and to assert that they are obligated to know justice. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is certainly your responsibility to know justice!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how to act justly]

2.note: Micah is using the adjectives **good** and **evil** as nouns to mean certain kinds of actions. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [doing good things and love doing evil things]

2.q: גֹּזְלֵ֤י עוֹרָ⁠ם֙ מֵֽ⁠עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וּ⁠שְׁאֵרָ֖⁠ם מֵ⁠עַ֥ל עַצְמוֹתָֽ⁠ם
2.note: Here Micah is speaking of the way the leaders oppress the people as if the leaders were butchers **tearing their skin from upon them and their flesh from upon their bones**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [brutally oppressing the people, taking everything they have]

The pronouns **their** and **them** refer to the victims of the leaders’ oppression. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people’s skin from upon them and the people’s flesh from upon their bones]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and tearing their flesh from upon their bones]

3.note: Here Micah is speaking of the way the leaders exploit the people as if the leaders had **eaten the flesh of my people**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and who have exploited my people]

Here Micah is speaking of how the leaders oppress the people as if the leaders had stripped **their skin from upon them** and had broken **their bones**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they have cruelly oppressed and crushed them]

Even though Micah is addressing the leaders of Israel directly (see 3:1), here he is speaking of them in the third person as **they**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person for consistency. Alternate translation: [you have stripped, and their bones you have broken, and you have chopped them up]

3.q: וּ⁠פָרְשׂוּ֙ כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּ⁠סִּ֔יר וּ⁠כְ⁠בָשָׂ֖ר בְּ⁠ת֥וֹךְ קַלָּֽחַת
3.note: The point of this comparison is that the leaders treat the people as cruelly as a cook treats the meat that he chops up to cook **as what is in the pot** and **as flesh inside a cauldron**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and they have chopped them up as cruelly as a cook chops up the meat that goes in the pot and the flesh inside a cauldron]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and as they chopped up the flesh to cook inside a cauldron]

4.note: The word **Then** indicates that these events will take place at a later time, after the wrongdoing described in the previous verses. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [At a later time]

4.q: וְ⁠יַסְתֵּ֨ר פָּנָ֤י⁠ו מֵ⁠הֶם֙ בָּ⁠עֵ֣ת הַ⁠הִ֔יא כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵרֵ֖עוּ מַעַלְלֵי⁠הֶֽם
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since they have made their deeds evil, he will hide his face from them at that time.]
The pronoun **they** refers to the leaders whom Micah has just finished addressing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the leaders will cry out]

The pronouns **he** and **his** refer to Yahweh, and the pronoun **them** refers to the leaders. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will hide his face from those leaders]

Here, **his face** represents Yahweh’s favorable attention, so that to **hide his face** means to refuse to help. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And he will refuse to help them]

5.note: Micah is using the words **Thus says Yahweh** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Yahweh is speaking of the prophets leading the people into wrong belief and behavior as if the prophets were **causing** the people **to wander astray** from the right path. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [causing my people to believe and act wrongly]

Yahweh is speaking of the practice the prophets had of giving a favorable prophecy to someone in exchange for food or payment as if they were **biting with their teeth**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when they have been given food to eat, then they call out, ‘Peace!’]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [You will live peacefully and be safe]

The implication is that the prophets perform religious ceremonies to declare a holy war against anyone who does not feed them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they perform ceremonies to declare a holy war against him]

The pronoun **they** refers to the prophets, and the pronoun **him** refers to anyone who does not give the prophets food. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the prophets consecrate war against that person]

6.note: The word **Therefore** indicates that what follows is the sentence for the crime the prophets are being accused of in the previous verse. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result. Alternate translation: [Because you have done these things]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the prophets losing their ability to receive revelation as if they would become blind, saying it would become **night for you**, a time **without vision**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you prophets will receive no more visions]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vision**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [without the ability to see visions]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know **divining** refers to the pagan practice these prophets used to predict the future. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and you will lose the ability you claim you have to predict the future]

6.q: וּ⁠בָ֤אָה הַ⁠שֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ עַל־הַ⁠נְּבִיאִ֔ים וְ⁠קָדַ֥ר עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֖ם הַ⁠יּֽוֹם
6.note: Yahweh is speaking of the prophets losing his favor and guidance and the gift of true prophesy as if the **sun will go down on the prophets**, and **the day will become dark over them**, leaving them in darkness. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the prophets will lose my guidance and the ability to see my revelation]

Even though Yahweh is addressing the prophets directly, here he is speaking of them in the third person as **the prophets** and **them**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a respectful form in the second person. Alternate translation: [on you prophets, and the day will become dark over you]

7.note: The expression **will be disgraced** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the diviners will no longer have honor from the people because they are unable to predict the future]

Covering the upper lip, represented here by **cover over the mustache**, was a symbolic action by which people showed that they were unclean or in mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And all of them will cover their upper lip to express their sorrow and shame]

Here Micah is using the possessive form to describe an **answer** that comes from **God**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [answer from God]

8.note: Micah uses the words **But** and **in contrast** here to indicate a contrast between the false prophets, who will be put to shame, and himself, who is empowered by the Spirit of Yahweh. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I, however, am full of]

Micah is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I am full** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize how he is different from the other prophets mentioned previously. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [In contrast to them, I am full]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **power**, **justice**, and **might**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [what makes me strong, the Spirit of Yahweh, and what makes me just and mighty]

Here Micah is using the possessive form to describe the **Spirit** that comes from and belongs to **Yahweh**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Spirit that comes from Yahweh]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You could supply these words if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I am full of the Spirit of Yahweh]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [to declare to the people of Israel how thy have rebelled by sinning again God]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **transgression** and **sin**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [about how he has rebelled and to Israel about how he has sinned]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. It may be helpful to repeat some of these words from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: [and to declare to Israel his sin]

9.q: רָאשֵׁי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּ⁠קְצִינֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
9.note: See how you translated the very similar phrases in [verse1](ta:03).
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is just]

Here Micah is speaking of what is morally right as if it were **straight**, and of corrupting it as if it were making it **crooked**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [corrupting everything that is right]

10.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in poetry, and follow that approach here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [building Zion with bloodshed, indeed, building Jerusalem with injustice]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and building Jerusalem with injustice]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **injustice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by doing what is unjust]

11.q: רָאשֶׁ֣י⁠הָ ׀ בְּ⁠שֹׁ֣חַד יִשְׁפֹּ֗טוּ וְ⁠כֹהֲנֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ בִּ⁠מְחִ֣יר יוֹר֔וּ וּ⁠נְבִיאֶ֖י⁠הָ בְּ⁠כֶ֣סֶף יִקְסֹ֑מוּ וְ⁠עַל־יְהוָה֙ יִשָּׁעֵ֣נוּ
11.note: Even though Micah has been addressing the various leaders of Jerusalem directly, here he is speaking of them in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person for consistency. Alternate translation: [You leaders judge for a bribe, and you priests teach for a price, and you prophets divine for silver. Yet you lean on Yahweh]

Here, **heads** represents the leaders of the city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Her leaders judge for a bribe]
The pronoun **Her** refers to the city of Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Jerusalem’s heads]

The pronoun **they** refers to the leaders, priests, and prophets of the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yet these same leaders, priests, and prophets lean on Yahweh]

Here Micah is speaking of trusting in Yahweh for support as if the people could physically **lean on Yahweh**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yet they claim to rely on Yahweh]

The leaders are using the question form to express their confidence that Yahweh is present with them and will protect them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Surely Yahweh is in our midst!]

12.note: The word **Therefore** indicates that what follows is the sentence for the crime the leaders are being accused of in the previous verses. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result. Alternate translation: [Because you have done these things]

The pronoun **you** refers to the leaders, priests, and prophets of the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [because of you leaders, priests, and prophets]

12.q: צִיּ֖וֹן שָׂדֶ֣ה תֵֽחָרֵ֑שׁ וִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עִיִּ֣ין תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְ⁠הַ֥ר הַ⁠בַּ֖יִת לְ⁠בָמ֥וֹת יָֽעַר
12.note: See how you translated these phrases quoted in Jeremiah 26:18.

The point of this comparison is that Zion, or Jerusalem will be so completely destroyed that the ground where the city stood will be **plowed** like an open **field**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Zion will be so completely leveled that it will be like a plowed field]

The expression **will be plowed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who does the action, it is the enemies of Zion who will plow it. Alternate translation: [your enemies will plow Zion like a field]

Micah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the mountain of the house will become as high places of a forest]

Here Micah is speaking of the temple as if it were a **house**, since it was the place where Yahweh was present among his people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the temple mountain]

Here Micah is using the possessive form to describe **high places** that are characterized by being overgrown like a **forest**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as high places overgrown with forest]
